package_info.package_manager: custom/.NET binary (not a public package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: HYPERSCRAPE is a custom-built data extraction tool attributed to the Charming Kitten APT group, designed specifically to automate unauthorized access and exfiltration of email data from compromised Gmail, Yahoo, and Outlook accounts. It performs a series of malicious actions including user agent spoofing, automated login with stolen credentials, changing account settings, bulk downloading of emails, deleting security alerts, and optionally requesting Google Takeout exports, all without user consent. Its sole function is to facilitate cyber espionage and large-scale data theft.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after attacker logs in with stolen credentials)
required_permissions: authenticated access to victim email account

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sets the user agent to mimic an outdated browser and logs into the victim's email account using stolen credentials, enabling session hijacking and evasion of some security controls.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Spoofing the user agent to appear as an outdated browser and automating login with stolen credentials are classic techniques for bypassing security controls and concealing automated access.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate email clients do not spoof user agents to outdated browsers nor automate logins with credentials obtained via phishing.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testing tools may use similar techniques for authorized red team operations, but only with explicit consent.
key_indicators: User agent string set to outdated browser
Automated login with externally supplied credentials
Absence of user interaction during login

required_permissions: authenticated access to victim email account

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code changes the victim's email account language to English, standardizing the interface for reliable automated parsing and extraction of email data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Changing the account language without user consent is a strong indicator of automated, unauthorized access intended to facilitate data extraction.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate clients do not change account language settings as part of normal operation, especially without user interaction.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Migration or backup tools may temporarily change language for data export, but only with user consent and notification.

required_permissions: authenticated access to victim email account

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code iterates through all emails in the victim's inbox, downloads each message as an .eml file to local storage, and marks them as unread, enabling bulk exfiltration of email data while minimizing user suspicion.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Bulk downloading of all emails and marking them as unread is not typical user behavior and is indicative of automated data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal email clients do not mass-download all emails in .eml format nor manipulate read/unread status in this way without user direction.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Email migration or backup tools may perform similar actions, but only with explicit user consent and notification.
key_indicators: Automated marking of emails as unread

required_permissions: authenticated access to victim email account

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code restores the victim's email account language to its original setting after data extraction, attempting to conceal evidence of tampering and reduce the likelihood of detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Restoring account settings to their original state is a common anti-forensics technique used to avoid detection after malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate clients do not revert language settings after automated operations, especially without user awareness.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some migration tools may restore settings post-operation, but only with user consent and transparency.
key_indicators: No user notification of setting change

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after data extraction and language restoration)
required_permissions: authenticated access to victim email account

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// Pseudocode representation
DeleteEmails(where subject contains 'security alert' and sender is Google);
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code searches for and deletes security alert emails from Google in the victim's inbox, suppressing notifications that could alert the victim to unauthorized access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deleting security alert emails is a clear attempt to prevent the victim from discovering the compromise and ongoing malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate email clients do not selectively delete security notifications or alerts from service providers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use case exists for targeted deletion of security alert emails without user direction.
key_indicators: Targeted deletion of emails with 'security alert' in subject

required_permissions: authenticated access to victim email account

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code requests a Google Takeout export of the victim's account data and downloads the resulting archive, enabling comprehensive exfiltration of all available account data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated Google Takeout requests and downloads are not typical user behavior and can result in large-scale, unauthorized data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal users initiate Takeout exports manually and are notified by Google; automated, silent requests are highly suspicious.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate users may use Google Takeout for personal backups, but always with manual initiation and notification.

attack_chain.action: Attacker logs into the victim's email account using stolen credentials and spoofs the user agent to appear as an outdated browser.
attack_chain.leads_to: Gains authenticated session for further actions

attack_chain.action: Changes the account language to English to standardize the interface for automated extraction.
attack_chain.leads_to: Enables reliable parsing and extraction of emails

attack_chain.action: Downloads all emails as .eml files and marks them as unread.
Restores the account language to its original setting to avoid detection.
Deletes security alert emails from Google to suppress notifications.
attack_chain.leads_to: Prevents victim from being alerted to compromise

attack_chain.action: Optionally, requests and downloads a Google Takeout export for comprehensive data theft (in earlier versions).

behavioral_signatures: Automated login to webmail with user agent spoofed to outdated browser
Bulk download of emails as .eml files to local storage
Automated change and restoration of account language settings
Targeted deletion of security alert emails from Google
Automated Google Takeout export requests and archive downloads
file_indicators: Presence of .eml files in attacker-controlled directories
HYPERSCRAPE binary hashes (as provided in IOCs)
network_indicators: Unusual login activity from attacker infrastructure IPs
Automated requests to Google Takeout endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unusual login activity, especially with outdated browser user agents and from suspicious IP addresses. Alert on bulk email downloads as .eml files, automated changes to account language settings, and deletion of security alert emails from Google. Correlate with known HYPERSCRAPE binary hashes and C2 IP addresses. Detect automated Google Takeout export requests and archive downloads not initiated by the user.
